rulebook.title: Shogi Rulebook & Tactics Notes
rulebook.subtitle: From piece movements and foul rules to customizable tactical study notes
rulebook.disclaimer_text: Note: Castles and tactical descriptions are starter templates generated by AI. Feel free to edit them with your own research or open positions in Studio to analyze and record moves.
rulebook.btn_open_studio: Open in Studio to Record Moves
rulebook.field_tag: Category / Tag (e.g., Static Rook, Ranging Rook)
rulebook.recorder_heading: Record Position & Moves (Click pieces on board)
rulebook.reset_confirm: Reset all tactical notes to default starter templates? Your custom changes will be lost.
rulebook.sanyata_summary: When the exact same board position occurs 4 times, the game is declared a draw.
rulebook.sanyata_condition_1: Identical placement of all pieces on the 9x9 board
rulebook.sanyata_condition_2: Identical pieces in hand for both players
rulebook.perpetual_check_desc: If a player causes repetition through a continuous series of checks, that player immediately forfeits by foul.
rulebook.impasse_summary: When both Kings enter enemy camps and cannot be checkmated, game result is decided by point counting.
rulebook.impasse_point_title: Points Counting (Pieces in Enemy Camp + Hand)
rulebook.illustrations_subtitle: Create and edit partial Shogi board diagrams (1x1 to 9x9) with highlights, markers, and arrows for tesuji explanations.
rulebook.default_fundoshi_desc: Dropping a Knight to fork Rook and Gold (or Bishop and Gold) at the same time.
rulebook.default_atama_desc: Dropping Gold directly in front of the enemy King to deliver checkmate.
rulebook.piece_king_desc: Moves 1 square in any of the 8 surrounding directions. Cannot promote; losing it loses the game.
rulebook.piece_rook_desc: Slides any distance orthogonally. Promotes to Dragon, also moving 1 square diagonally.
rulebook.piece_bishop_desc: Slides any distance diagonally. Promotes to Horse, also moving 1 square orthogonally.
rulebook.piece_gold_desc: Moves 1 square orthogonally or diagonally forward (cannot move diagonally backward or promote).
rulebook.piece_silver_desc: Moves 1 square forward or diagonally in any direction. Promotes to move like a Gold.
rulebook.piece_knight_desc: Jumps 2 squares forward and 1 square sideways over pieces. Promotes to move like a Gold.
rulebook.piece_lance_desc: Slides any distance straight forward. Promotes to move like a Gold.
rulebook.piece_pawn_desc: Moves 1 square straight forward. Promotes to Tokin, moving like a Gold.

tree_page.title: Joseki Tree
tree_page.subtitle: Unified opening tree merging pro games with your own studies and sparring matches

guide.title: User Guide
guide.subtitle: Pick a screen or topic to read detailed instructions

quickstart.title: Get Started in 3 Steps
quickstart.short_desc: Import kifu -> Analyze & branch -> Save and grow your tree
quickstart.intro: No account or setup is required. Follow these three steps to start building your opening repertoire.
quickstart.step1_title: Step 1: Import a Game (or Try a Sample)
quickstart.step1_body: Open Import Kifu from the Study Board header or mobile bottom nav. Paste KIF/CSA/JKF text, pick files/folders, or tap a sample game to start immediately.
quickstart.step2_body: Use the AI Analysis tab powered by Fairy-Stockfish to inspect candidate moves, PV lines, and eval graphs. Playing an alternative move at any ply automatically adds a branch.
quickstart.step3_title: Step 3: Save to Your Library & Opening Tree
quickstart.step3_body: Save or save-as-new from the Kifu Management modal. Saved games appear in Kifu Library for filtering and are merged automatically into the Joseki Tree.
quickstart.reassurance_body: All kifu records, notes, and settings stay inside your browser on your device. Everything works offline, and no kifu data is ever sent to a developer server.

tree.title: Joseki Tree Visualizer
tree.short_desc: Merged variations, scope toggles, color legend, and position jumps
tree.intro: All saved games are merged from ply 0 into one interactive tree so you can compare mainlines and sidelines at a glance.
tree.card1_body: Switch between Pro Only, Self Only, and All at the top right. In All mode, emerald shows shared lines played by both pro and your games, sky shows pro-only lines, and amber shows your own study or sparring lines. Thicker branches represent more games.
tree.card2_body: Choose how deep the tree renders (15 / 25 / 35 / 50 plies). Drag the canvas to pan and use the mouse wheel or +, -, and Reset buttons to inspect dense branches comfortably.
tree.card3_title: 3. Jump from Any Node to Study Board
tree.card3_body: Click any node to see the games passing through that position and their next moves, then open the Study Board directly at that exact ply to analyze or spar.

study.title: Study Board, AI Analysis & Variations
study.short_desc: Candidate moves, eval graphs, automatic branching, and Position Editor
study.card1_body: Step through moves via the left kifu tree or arrow keys. Playing a different move from any ply creates a new variation branch cleanly without overwriting the mainline.
study.card2_body: Run AI analysis on the right panel to view evaluation bars, board arrows, and clickable PV lines. Full-game analysis builds an evaluation timeline showing blunders and turning points.
study.card3_body: Toggle edit mode on the kifu tree to prune sidelines or promote variations. Save updated lines anytime from Kifu Management.
study.card4_body: Open Menu -> Edit Position or Library -> New Position to place, remove, flip, or promote pieces freely, clear the board to the box, and create tsumego or study diagrams.

import.title: Kifu Import, Bulk Load & Saving
import.short_desc: Text paste, multi-file/folder bulk import, duplicate checks, Save vs Save as New
import.card1_title: 1. Paste Text or Test Sample Games
import.card1_body: Paste KIF, KI2, CSA, or JKF text, review the live preview, and save straight into the Study Board. Built-in sample games let you try every feature in one click.
import.card2_body: Drag and drop multiple files or whole folders at once. Legacy Japanese encodings are detected automatically, and duplicate games are skipped safely before saving.
import.card3_body: Search saved games, rename titles and tags inline, and select multiple games for sequential background AI analysis.
import.card4_body: When saving new study branches, choose whether to overwrite the active game or save a separate copy with a new title and tags.

library.title: Kifu Library & Players Encyclopedia
library.short_desc: Category tabs, compound/My Filters, Tag Dictionary, Player stats, Trash
library.card1_body: Switch between All, Pro, Ladies, Amateur, and Self games, or open dedicated sections for Tsumego, Next-Move Quizzes, and Saved Diagrams.
library.card2_title: Compound Filters, My Filters & Tag Dictionary
library.card2_body: Combine filters for openings, winners, turn, analysis status, and tags, and save frequent searches as 1-click My Filters. Use Tag Management to rename or merge tags.
library.card3_body: Deleted games move to Trash so you can restore them anytime instead of losing data permanently.
library.card4_body: Automatically aggregates game counts, win rates, and opening tendencies per player. Merge duplicate spellings, reclassify AI engines, or edit player categories.

tactics.title: Tactics Notes, Split Study & Opening Books
tactics.short_desc: Tactics collections, board diagrams, Split Study, and .db/.sbk books
tactics.card1_body: Create dedicated notebooks for openings, castles, and attacking plans with pros/cons, key lines, and embedded board diagrams.
tactics.card2_body: Enable Split Study on the Study Board to display tactics notes, opening books, web references, or memos side by side with the live board.
tactics.card3_body: Register YaneuraOu or ShogiHome compatible .db / .sbk opening books in Settings -> AI Engine to look up book candidates, win rates, and frequencies per position.
tactics.card4_body: Capture partial sequences directly via KIF Snippet import, or export and share tactics note bundles with other devices.

training.title: Sparring, Quiz, Tsumego & Trace
training.short_desc: AI sparring, blunder quizzes, .sfen/.kif tsumego, and move tracing
training.intro: Switch tabs on the Study Board to turn any studied position or saved game into interactive training.
training.mode1_body: Play against AI from startpos or any study position, with configurable time controls and one-click merging of sparring lines into your tree.
training.mode2_body: Automatically extracts sharp turning points and mistakes from AI-analyzed games for progressive hint-assisted next-move drills.
training.mode3_body: Solve built-in problems, import external .sfen / .kif collections, filter by move length, or auto-extract missed mates from your analyzed games.
training.mode4_body: Replay saved pro or personal games move-by-move to build pattern recognition and memorize mainlines.

customize.title: Themes, Custom Assets, AI & Opening Books
customize.short_desc: Board/piece SVG, custom audio, NNUE/USI (.exe), .db/.sbk books
customize.section1_body: Switch board themes (Kaya, Wood, Dark, Slate) and 1-kanji / 2-kanji pieces in Settings -> Appearance. You can also upload custom board SVG/PNG, 8x4 piece sprite sheets, and move audio (MP3/WAV/OGG).
customize.sprite_hint: Arranged in an equal 8-column × 4-row grid (top 2 rows: Sente normal/promoted; bottom 2 rows: Gote rotated 180°). Download this SVG to use directly as your template.
customize.board_hint: Scaled to fit an ~11:12 (439×480) board area. Because the 9×9 grid lines, star points, and outer margin are drawn inside the image itself, editing based on the template above keeps every piece aligned cleanly.
customize.section2_body: In Settings -> AI Engine, add your own evaluation files (.nnue / .bin) in the browser, or connect local shogi engines (.exe such as YaneuraOu or Suisho) directly in the Windows Desktop app.
customize.section3_body: Load YaneuraOu / ShogiHome compatible .db or .sbk opening books in Settings -> AI Engine to inspect book candidates and win rates inside Split Study.

sync.title: Backup, Folder Sync & Cloud
sync.short_desc: File export/import, Drive/OneDrive folder sync, optional cloud sync
sync.intro: Choose from three backup and cross-device synchronization methods depending on your workflow.
sync.opt1_body: Export all kifu, settings, quizzes, matches, and review history to a single backup file in Settings -> Data Management and restore safely with duplicate-skipping merge.
sync.opt2_body: In desktop Chrome/Edge, select a shared folder (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox) to auto-merge on startup and auto-backup on exit without any cloud account setup.
sync.opt3_body: For advanced users who want automatic sync between PC and mobile: register your own cloud settings in Settings -> Account to sync across devices without relying on a third-party server.

faq.title: FAQ & Troubleshooting
faq.short_desc: App install, Windows SmartScreen, data safety, and licenses

items.q: Can I install this as a standalone app (Add to Home Screen)?
items.a: Yes. Use Safari's Add to Home Screen on mobile or the Install button in Chrome/Edge on desktop to run offline in standalone mode.

items.q: Why does Windows SmartScreen warn when launching the Desktop build?
items.a: Because this is a free, community-built open-source app without a commercial signing certificate, Windows may show SmartScreen on first launch. Click More Info -> Run Anyway to open it.

items.q: Will clearing browser site data erase my kifu?
items.a: Yes—because kifu and settings live inside your browser by default, clearing site data removes local data. Back up periodically via Settings -> Data Management or Folder Sync.

items.q: What if in-browser AI feels slow or unavailable?
items.a: Device performance or browser limits can slow down in-browser analysis. Lower the default browser search depth (8-10) in Settings or use a local engine via the Desktop app.

items.q: What licenses apply to imported kifu, books, or NNUE files?
items.a: Kiju is free open-source software (GNU GPL-3.0) and does not bundle external kifu, opening books, or AI weights. Please follow the terms of any external files you load.

items.q: Do you collect analytics or track usage?
items.a: On the public web release, cookieless anonymous usage statistics (Umami Cloud: page views, feature counts, and imported game counts) are recorded solely to improve the app. Kifu contents, player names, filenames, and personal data are never transmitted, and tracking is disabled offline or locally.
